subjects.displayTitle: Divine bounty: the gift that sustains existence
subjects.introduction: Fish swim in the sea and never see it; so, ‘Abdu’l‑Bahá says, do we live inside a bounty so constant that we forget to ask what holds us up. Bahá’u’lláh teaches that if the tide of divine grace were withheld for a single moment the world would cease, that existence is not a gift received once at the beginning but a current flowing now, like sunlight, breath or spring rain. Yet the sun is not the earth it warms: creation proceeds from God by emanation, as writing from a writer, without the Source becoming any of the things it sustains. That distinction between emanation and manifestation keeps the imagery from collapsing into pantheism, and it opens onto the soul as an emanation and the divine attributes hidden within every atom. Plotinus pictures an overflow that gives without being depleted [1], and Paul at Athens speaks of the God in whom all live and move [2]. Rain falls alike on fertile soil and barren, and the only true answer to such impartial generosity is a kindness that expects nothing in return.

order.why: Open with a vivid image of a dependence so pervasive it can be overlooked: fish within the ocean that sustains them.
shortened: Verily, divine bestowals are like the sea, and we are the fishes of that sea. The fishes must not look at themselves; they must behold the ocean, which is vast and wonderful. Provision for the sustenance of all is in this ocean; therefore, the divine bounties encompass all, and love eternal shines upon all.

order.why: Begin with the image of fish sustained by an ocean, then connect dependence, the distinction between source and creation, receptivity and impartial kindness.
shortened: Throughout the universe the divine power is effulgent in endless images and pictures. The world of creation, the world of humanity may be likened to the earth itself and the divine power to the sun. This Sun has shone upon all mankind. In the endless variety of its reflections the divine Will is manifested. Consider how all are recipients of the bounty of the same Sun.

order.why: Distinguish the divine signs from the divine Self before the imagery of oceans and rays is read as literal identity.
shortened: Every created being however revealeth His signs which are but emanations from Him and not His Own Self. All these signs are reflected and can be seen in the book of existence, and the scrolls that depict the shape and pattern of the universe are indeed a most great book.
Consider the rays of the sun whose light hath encompassed the world. The rays emanate from the sun and reveal its nature, but are not the sun itself.

order.why: Keep the actual question concerning God and creation with the answer.
shortened: Question: What is the nature of the connection between God and His creation, between the Absolute and Inaccessible One and all other beings?
Answer: The connection between God and His creation is that of the originator and the originated, of the sun and the dark bodies of the universe, of the craftsman and his handiwork.

The procession of creation from God is a procession through emanation; that is, creation emanates from God, it does not manifest Him. The connection is that of emanation and not of manifestation. The light of the sun emanates from the sun, it does not manifest it.

order.why: Make the ethical consequence of universal bounty concrete through unconditional charity, including the warning against covert conversion.
shortened: Rays of sunlight, the heat of the sun, or the falling rain of divine bounty are bestowed unconditionally and without any ulterior motive. In the same manner, a Baha'i must be the manifestation of divine generosity and charity.

Answer: Know that procession is of two kinds: procession and appearance through emanation and procession and appearance through manifestation. Emanational procession is like the procession of the handiwork from its author. For example, the writing proceeds from the writer. Now, just as the writing emanates from the writer and the discourse from the speaker, so does the human spirit emanate from God.

But what we mean is emanational realization, like rays emanating from the sun. Similarly, created things have emanated from that True Existence. Thus created things are from Him, not Him.

The first emanation is the outpouring grace of the Kingdom, which has emanated from God and has appeared in the realities of all things, even as the rays emanating from the sun are reflected in all things. And that grace---the rays---appears in infinite forms in the realities of all things, and is specified and individuated according to their capacity, receptivity, and essence.

That is to say, its effulgent rays shine upon them all and they, in turn, reflect faithfully its light. Thus, if thou dost gaze upon the stone, the earth, the plant, the animal, and man, thou wilt find them one and all to be partaking of the bounty of the sun.

Therefore, all the objective phenomena are as surfaces of mirrors upon which the Sun of Truth has cast the rays of the Outpouring of Bounty.  All these surfaces (different stages of life) are mirrors reflecting the rays of the Sun of Truth.  The Outpouring is the One Outpouring, and the Effulgence is the One Effulgence.

And yet the peoples of the world have denied this grace!  Every tree hath been endowed with the choicest fruits, every ocean enriched with the most luminous gems.  Man, himself, hath been invested with the gifts of understanding and knowledge.  The whole creation hath been made the recipient of the revelation of the All-Merciful, and the earth the repository of things inscrutable to all except God, the Truth, the Knower of things unseen.

shortened: Originally a Mu'tazilite himself, like his famous contemporary and colleague, ar-Razi, his studies on the theory of knowledge led him more and more into the Kingdom of God (Malakut-i-Allah).

Ar-Razi is also a precursor of the Babi-Baha'i Teachings, in that he, as the first researcher, represented the Creator as well as the creation in the category of light: Our reason is light of the Light of God. Everything spiritual is a reflection of the Light of God. The creation is an emanation of light of the eternal Light.

questions: What does it mean to depend on divine bounty at every moment, rather than only at the beginning of existence? How do the ocean, sunlight, breath and flowing water bring different aspects of that dependence into view?

How do the explanations of emanation distinguish a source from what proceeds from it? Where do the metaphors help, and where might taking them literally produce a meaning the passages themselves reject?

How can bounty be universal while its reception varies? What do the passages about capacity, effort and freedom suggest about a person’s responsibility for growth without making grace something merely earned?

How do the texts connect the sustaining of all existence with the appearance of the Manifestations and the renewal of spiritual life? What changes when the winter image is read together with the return of spring?
What does receiving without exclusion ask of the way we give to others? How do unconditional charity, useful action and love reflected from heart to heart connect this subject with everyday life?

What becomes clearer when Plotinus and Acts are read beside these selections, and which distinctions remain essential? Which connected subject—the Holy Spirit, divine attributes within all things, the soul as emanation, or emanation versus manifestation—would help deepen your next inquiry?

references.label: 1 · Plotinus, Enneads V.2 · Giving without depletion
references.note: Plotinus describes the One as the source of all things without identifying it with any one thing. His metaphor of overflow leads through Intellect and Soul; he cautions that this procession is not a movement through space. Compare the passage with the sun-and-rays analogy and the distinction between emanation and manifestation. How can a source give without becoming divided or diminished? The Neoplatonic sequence has its own structure and should not be treated as identical to the Baha’i account of God, Command and creation.
references.verified: Read both sections of Enneads V.2 in full on 2026-10-10 in the Stephen MacKenna and B. S. Page translation hosted by Wabash College, including the explicit metaphor of overflow, the sequence of Intellect and Soul, and the rejection of spatial interpretation.

references.label: 2 · Acts 17:24–29 · Life received, nearness sought
references.note: This passage presents God as the giver of life and breath to all, brings the nations within a common origin, and joins the search for God to divine nearness. It also rejects reducing the divine to an image fashioned from material things. Read it beside the compilation’s language of continuing dependence and its call to treat every person with mercy. What might a shared source imply for human relationships? The Christian speech provides a comparison of dependence and nearness, rather than a technical account of emanation.
references.verified: Read Acts 17:24–29 in full in the King James Version on Bible Gateway on 2026-10-10, including life and breath, common human origin, the search for God, nearness and the rejection of manufactured images.
